taxonomy.subtopic: 21-hydroxylase deficiency with salt wasting and androgen excess

questions.stem_html: A newborn with a 46,XX karyotype has virilized external genitalia. On day 8 of life, the infant develops vomiting, hypotension, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone is markedly elevated. The accompanying steroid pathway shows the blocked step. Which pattern of adrenal products is most likely?

options.text_html: Decreased cortisol and aldosterone with increased adrenal androgen synthesis
Increased cortisol and aldosterone with decreased adrenal androgen synthesis
Decreased cortisol with increased aldosterone and decreased androgens
Increased cortisol with decreased aldosterone and increased androgens
Normal cortisol and aldosterone with isolated reduction in catecholamines

questions.explanation_html: 21-hydroxylase is required in both cortisol and mineralocorticoid pathways. Severe deficiency lowers cortisol and aldosterone synthesis. Loss of cortisol feedback increases ACTH, causing adrenal hyperplasia and accumulation of 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Precursors are diverted into androgen synthesis, causing virilization. Aldosterone deficiency produces sodium loss, volume depletion, hyperkalemia, and salt wasting.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: The blocked enzyme prevents normal cortisol and aldosterone synthesis.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Aldosterone is reduced in the salt-wasting form, and androgen production increases.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Cortisol is deficient because 21-hydroxylation is required to form 11-deoxycortisol.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: The adrenal medulla is not the primary site of the steroidogenic defect.

questions.educational_objective: Severe 21-hydroxylase deficiency decreases cortisol and aldosterone, increases ACTH and 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and diverts precursors toward androgen production.

media.alt_text: Simplified adrenal steroid pathway showing a 21-hydroxylase block, reduced cortisol and aldosterone, and increased androgen production.
